cpp-block.comment: Raw C++ escape hatch: `cpp { … }`. The body is highlighted as C++ (source.cpp), with balanced-brace tracking so the closing brace is matched correctly.
cpp-block.name: meta.embedded.block.cpp.cheatah

cpp-braces.comment: Consume a balanced { … } region inside a cpp block so inner braces don't end the block early.

patterns.comment: The module path in an import: `import math`, `import os.path`.
A known stdlib module used as a `module.` prefix (e.g. the `math` in `math.sqrt`).
patterns.name: entity.name.namespace.cheatah

template-construct.comment: Explicit template construction/call `Type<Args>(…)`, e.g. `MemoryStore<ndarray, 1024, 2>(…)`: color the capitalized type name and its template arguments — type names AND non-type integer literals (the fixed-size defaults). The `(?=…>\s*\()` lookahead commits ONLY when the angle list closes and is immediately followed by `(`, so an ordinary `a < b` comparison is left untouched.

template-call.comment: A method/function call with explicit template arguments: `name<Args>(…)`, e.g. `obj.get<int>(…)`. The name (any case, including lowercase method calls) is colored as a call; capitalized `Type<Args>(…)` construction is handled first by #template-construct. The `(?=…>\s*\()` lookahead commits ONLY when the angle list closes immediately before `(`, so an ordinary `a < b` comparison is left untouched.

patterns.comment: Dual scope: default VS Code themes leave plain keyword.operator uncolored; keyword.operator.wordlike is their hook for word-shaped operators (same trick as keyword.operator.logical.python), so and/or/not color like keywords.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.logical.cheatah keyword.operator.wordlike.cheatah

patterns.comment: Function declaration with its parameter list as a region: inside `(...)` a colon is always a `: Type` annotation, so types can be colored without misreading slice/dict colons in ordinary code.
patterns.name: meta.function.parameters.cheatah

patterns.comment: A fn declaration whose `(` hasn't been typed yet — keep the name colored while editing.

type-annotation.comment: `: Type` after a parameter name. Ends before `,` (next param), `)` (list end), `=` (default value), or end of line. Generic-argument commas are shielded by #type-brackets.

type-expression.comment: A type per the parser: IDENT ( '[' (type | NUMBER) (',' …)* ']' )? — e.g. Response, list[int], array[float, 3]. Builtins keep support.type; everything else is a user type.

type-brackets.comment: Balanced `[...]` of generic arguments, so its commas don't end the enclosing annotation.

param-default.comment: `= expr` default value in a parameter list, highlighted as a normal expression. Nested call parens are shielded by #balanced-parens so their commas/`)` don't end the default or the parameter list early.

patterns.comment: ALL-CAPS names read as constants/enum values — WITH or WITHOUT underscores, so `MTL_IN`, `OUT`, `SYMS`, `VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_APPLICATION_INFO` all color the same. The ≥2-char all-uppercase shape (ending in a letter/digit) leaves PascalCase type names (VkApplicationInfo) alone, since those contain lowercase letters.
patterns.name: constant.other.caps.cheatah

_generic-comment.comment: Rainbow nesting for C++20-style generic type arguments `Type<...>`. The type name and its angle brackets are colored by NESTING DEPTH (level 1/2/3, then 4 for everything deeper), via four mutually-recursive rules. The begin lookahead `(?=[A-Za-z0-9_,\s<>\[\]]*>)` commits only when a `>` actually closes the angle list (so an ordinary `a < b` comparison is left alone).

patterns.comment: Builtin type names — but NOT when called like a function/constructor (`str(x)`, `int(5)`): the trailing-`(` lookahead leaves those to #function-call so they color as a call, while `: str` / `list[int]` color as a type.
patterns.name: support.type.cheatah

function-call.comment: An identifier immediately followed by `(` is a call.
function-call.name: entity.name.function.call.cheatah

patterns.comment: Unary address-of (passed through to C++ for C interop, e.g. `&info`).
patterns.name: keyword.operator.address-of.cheatah

designated-initializer.comment: C++20 designated initializer, e.g. `Type({ .field = value, … })` — the modern Vulkan struct-construction style, valid across multiple lines. Committed only when `{` is immediately followed by `.field`, so ordinary code blocks (`if x { … }`, fn bodies) are left untouched. The body is highlighted as normal cheatah ($self), with the leading `.field` of each designator colored as a member; nested designated initializers recurse so an inner `}` never closes the outer one early.

patterns.comment: A designator `.field =` (the field is followed by `=`). The `(?=\s*=)` lookahead is essential: WITHOUT it this matched any `.member`, so a method call inside a value (e.g. `.w = ndarray.zeros(...)` — the `.zeros`) was mis-colored as a designator instead of a method.
patterns.name: variable.other.member.designator.cheatah

member-constant.comment: `.SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` member — a namespaced enum value / constant, e.g. `vk.STRUCTURE_TYPE_APPLICATION_INFO`, `vk.API_VERSION_1_3`. Colored like a constant, matching how the bare `VK_*` form colors.

member-access.comment: `.member` field access on a value (e.g. `obj.field`, the `.sType` of a designated initializer). The negative lookahead leaves `.method(…)` calls to #function-call (so `vk.CreateInstance()` and `io.print()` color as calls, not plain members), and `.SCREAMING` constants to #member-constant. The dot stays plain punctuation.
